intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that syndromic congenital fibrosis of extraocular muscles-3A-2 with joint contractures, developmental delay, and peripheral neuropathy (CFEOM3A2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TUBB3 gene (602661) on chromosome 16q24.3.

paragraphs.text: CFEOM3A2, also called the TUBB3 R262H syndrome, presents at birth with ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, exotropia, facial weakness, facial dysmorphism and, in most cases, distal congenital joint contractures. Affected individuals later develop intellectual disability, gait disorders with proximal joint contractures, Kallmann syndrome, and a progressive peripheral neuropathy during the first decade of life. Whitman et al. (2021) considered it the most debilitating of the CFEOM-TUBB3 syndromes described to date.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) studied participants from 3 families who carried TUBB3 R262H or D417H substitutions. All had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness. All were born with congenital wrist and finger contractures, which the authors suggested reflected maldevelopment of spinal motor neurons. In the first decade of life they developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss. Electromyography showed a chronic, generalized, predominantly axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, which had been diagnosed as CMT2 in some subjects.

paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) reported that patients from 2 families with the R262H substitution had severe CFEOM3, facial weakness, and congenital ulnar deviation of the hand with contractures of the thumbs and fingers. Brain MRI showed diffuse hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, agenesis of the anterior commissure, a hypoplastic anterior limb of the internal capsule, and dysmorphic basal ganglia. Individuals with R262H had mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments. The twin of an R262H patient had dysgenesis of both anterior limbs of the internal capsule, apparent fusion of an enlarged left caudate head with the putamen, and dilatation of both anterior horns of the lateral ventricles. R262H subjects also had hypoplasia of the left caudate body and tail. No scan showed cortical dysplasia or evidence of a cortical migration defect. Brain imaging was not reviewed for any D417H subject.

paragraphs.text: Whitman et al. (2021) described 14 individuals from 13 unrelated families with the TUBB3 R262H variant. All presented as newborns with profound bilateral limitation of eye movements, large exotropia and facial weakness, and 13 had distal joint contractures at birth. Ten had fetal distress, which led to premature delivery in 3, and 3 were small for gestational age or had intrauterine growth restriction. Eight had vocal cord paralysis needing tracheostomy shortly after birth, 9 needed nasogastric or gastrostomy tube feeding in infancy, and 2 had congenital unilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Failure to thrive and short stature were common: 11 subjects were below average height, 13 were below average weight, and 6 had microcephaly. All had facial dysmorphism and facial weakness; 3D photographic analysis of 4 subjects showed reduced facial depth, nasal protrusion, upper facial height, vertical lip dimensions and palpebral fissure length, with normal or increased intercanthal width.

paragraphs.text: All 14 subjects reported by Whitman et al. (2021) had varying degrees of global developmental delay, with speech comprehension and communication better than other domains. Full-scale IQ in the 5 subjects tested at NIH ranged from 17 to 96. The monozygotic twins had autism spectrum disorder. Ten subjects were left-handed, and 3 had seizures or epileptic activity that needed antiepileptic therapy. Gross motor milestones were delayed in all. Of the 9 subjects older than 5 years, 4 learned to walk unassisted and 5 needed assistive devices, and motor function generally worsened by adolescence. Although hypotonia had been reported in all at some point, subjects examined at NIH had proximal or hip-girdle weakness. Some had extensor plantar responses with ankle clonus, which the authors considered consistent with spasticity combined with peripheral neuropathy.

Some subjects had Sylvian fissure asymmetry (with polymicrogyria in 1), hippocampal malrotation, decreased white matter volume, or a small pons. paragraphs.text: Whitman et al. (2021) found that all subjects had at least 1 feature of Kallmann syndrome. paragraphs.text: Tischfield et al. (2010) expressed mutant TUBB3 in rabbit reticulocyte lysate and found that R262H, E410K, D417H and D417N heterodimers formed at moderate yields and co-cycled with native tubulin as efficiently as wildtype. In yeast, the R262H and D417H substitutions both caused a significant decrease in Kip3p and Kip2p kinesin accumulation on microtubule plus-ends, and the authors suggested that kinesin-microtubule interactions are reduced in humans carrying these substitutions. Deleting one copy of TUB2 in yeast caused benomyl sensitivity, whereas the disease substitutions conferred benomyl resistance. They concluded that the TUBB3 syndrome mutations mainly alter microtubule function in a dominant fashion, although partial loss of function could not be excluded for some, and proposed that the progressive axonal neuropathy results from secondary defects in motor protein transport.

paragraphs.text: Whitman et al. (2021) observed that substantial physical therapy from infancy was associated with the best motor outcomes. paragraphs.text: In patients from 2 unrelated pedigrees with severe CFEOM3, facial weakness, congenital hand contractures, brain malformations and early-onset axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, Tischfield et al. (2010) identified a heterozygous 785G-A transition in the TUBB3 gene, resulting in an arg262-to-his (R262H) substitution. The mutation arose de novo in each case, as sporadic disease or from presumed germline mosaicism; it was absent from the parents of sporadic individuals and was not found on more than 1700 control chromosomes. In yeast, heterozygous R262H microtubules had prolonged growth events, reduced rescue frequency, a decreased polymerization rate and an increased depolymerization rate, and decreased kinesin accumulation on microtubule plus-ends.
